associations.rationale: The equivalence says the partition-indexed Schur module is zero exactly when N is smaller than the number of parts, directly matching the theorem's vanishing clause.
This is the complementary nonvanishing reformulation of the vanishing criterion; it is useful context but is a consequence rather than the displayed zero-if-and-only-if claim itself.

For an antitone N-component highest weight, the formal equality identifies the Schur module's formal character with the Schur polynomial, directly stating the character clause in its nonvanishing parameterization.
The formal equality gives the Schur module's dimension as weylDimension, the formalized Weyl product appearing in the source, so it directly states the dimension clause.
This conjunction directly packages all three source assertions for a partition: the vanishing criterion and, when the number of parts is at most N, the Schur character and Weyl dimension formulas.
Under the source's N-at-least-number-of-parts hypothesis, this equality directly gives the partition-indexed module's dimension by the Weyl dimension expression.
This characterizes when the numerical finrank is zero; it follows from the module-vanishing statement in the finite-dimensional setting but does not itself state that the representation is zero.
With the number-of-parts bound assumed, the equality directly identifies the partition-indexed module's formal character with the corresponding Schur polynomial.
